subject: Slate velocity health check — close-profile rebaseline & risk docket
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Milner <sarah.milner@apexhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Slate velocity health check — initial findings and proposed reprofile

Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for the sync this morning. Per our review of the MAP and the evaluation plan cadence, I've pulled together a short risk inventory and a proposed reprofile for the close date. High‑level: two evaluation gates (performance regression test and security evidence) are likely to push acceptance by ~3 weeks unless we (A) accelerate the perf runs with additional parallel capacity, or (B) reduce the initial acceptance scope to a phased cutover.

I've attached the redlined MAP (redwood_map_v1.xlsx) and a one‑page risk docket that outlines the gating items. Key asks from your side:
- Procurement confirmation on the timeline for PO/contract sign (current blocker).
- Security ETA for SOC evidence (security told us a 2‑week queue is possible).
- Whether ApexHealth can accept a phased acceptance window (minimal acceptance for core APIs on day 1, broader eval over +30 days).

If procurement can't commit to the proposed PO timeline by Wednesday EOD (my side: 5/12), we'll need to loop in an exec cadence to avoid a hard slip. Ben and Grace are cc'd for support on the fallback plan and to draft an escalation ladder.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) You confirm procurement signoff cadence and any internal review that requires extra time.
2) If procurement needs >7 business days, we schedule an exec sync (15‑20m) and present the phased cutover option.

Thanks — attaching the files for reference.

—
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood_map_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Sarah Milner <sarah.milner@apexhealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@apexhealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T11:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Slate velocity health check — initial findings and proposed reprofile

Hi Stephanie —

Appreciate the clear summary and the MAP doc. Quick update from our side: procurement has a scheduled vendor review on Thursday (5/13) but they will not sign until compliance clears the SOC/controls evidence — that queue is currently unknown and could be 7–12 business days. I attached the procurement snapshot that outlines our internal gating (procurement-snapshot.pdf).

We're open to a phased acceptance approach, but two points:
1) Our legal requires the final contract executed before any production traffic.
2) Security has flagged one third‑party data transfer control that must be resolved before acceptance of embeddings/exports.

I don't want to block progress — happy to join a short exec sync if that helps accelerate procurement. Do you have proposed times?

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Milner
Director, Platform Integrations — ApexHealth
sarah.milner@apexhealth.com
Attachment: procurement-snapshot.pdf (PDF)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Sarah Milner <sarah.milner@apexhealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Slate velocity health check — initial findings and proposed reprofile

Folks — looping in a targeted escalation pathway so we don't lose momentum. Quoting Sarah above: procurement review 5/13, security queue unknown (7–12bd). That combination creates a material risk to the current close target.

Proposal (short, actionable):
- Option A (preferred): Exec sync 5/12 or 5/13 to get procurement to commit to a PO issuance timeline (we bring VP Sales and Legal for quick clarifications).
- Option B (fallback): Proceed with a scoped phased cutover: Core API acceptance on original target ±3 days (limited throughput + non‑export features), remaining features roll over to a +30 day acceptance window. This reduces business disruption and allows us to ship incrementally.

I've drafted an escalation ladder below for the exec sync deck:
1) VP Product (Redwood) — scope tradeoffs and signoff to phased plan.
2) VP Sales (Redwood) — commercial concession / temporary SLA adjustments.
3) ApexHealth CTO / VP Ops — procurement / compliance commitment.

Action items for this thread:
- Stephanie: confirm whether we should push the exec sync this week and I'll pull the deck.
- Sarah: if procurement can commit any earlier milestone (even a conditional PO), please flag it here.

Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-05-12T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Slate velocity health check — close-profile rebaseline & exec ask

Thanks all — quick summary and next steps. Forwarding the consolidated asks and updated MAP (attached).

On Wed, May 11, 2027 at 15:45, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Folks — looping in a targeted escalation pathway so we don't lose momentum.
> Proposal: Exec sync 5/12 or 5/13 to get procurement to commit to a PO issuance timeline.

Action summary:
- Sarah: please confirm by EOD Wednesday (5/12) whether procurement can issue a conditional PO or provide a signed letter of intent; if not, we will proceed to schedule the exec sync with VPs.
- Ben: please prepare a 6‑slide exec deck with the phased cutover option and commercial levers we can offer (timeboxed credits, temporary SLA concessions).
- Grace: please prepare a minimal scope list for the core API acceptance (call out features that can be delayed without breaking initial customer workflows).

I've attached MAP_reprofile_v2.xlsx which contains two rebaseline scenarios (3‑week slip and phased cutover). If we don't get procurement confirmation by Wednesday EOD, I'll escalate to our VP Sales and request an ApexHealth CTO touchpoint.

Proposed exec sync slot: 2027-05-13 09:00–09:20 PT (calendar link: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=exec-sync-20270512).

Thanks — I will update HubSpot and the doc links after we hear back.
